decisions.default: vera.json competitorFOMO[] order: ServiceTitan, CE+SF, Document Crunch, McKinsey

Document Crunch's 'weeks to minutes' per contract review event exceeds all others in stated time magnitude. CE+SF ranks second: exact-match relevanceTier and directly names Ashley's documented 1.5h/job pain point — highest resonance for operational-pragmatist. ServiceTitan third: same upstream system (HD Portal), unquantified but ongoing weekly hours. McKinsey last: analytical percentage stat, not a task-elimination story — fomoProfileFit = roi-analytical (fits EB layer, not champion).

Operational-pragmatist fomoFraming requires leading with the specific person and the specific task that disappears. Rewrite leads with Ashley by name and names the exact contract set (HS-105, 299A, 299B, HS-118 — per sage.json) before framing the industry comparison. 'Go-live day' anchors the outcome to a concrete moment per profile requirement.

decisions.default: McKinsey's 2024 number: 14–15% productivity gain for data-driven construction firms vs. 0.4%/year for everyone else. The price of staying in the 0.4% bucket is paid by Ashley every morning.
decisions.chosen: Every morning Ashley spends on manual HD reconciliation, ComputerEase rekey, and document-by-document contract review is the operating cost of staying in construction's 0.4%/year productivity baseline. Data-driven contractors reach 14–15% productivity gains. That gap closes in Year 1.
decisions.rationale: Original opened with the McKinsey stat (roi-analytical hook — correct for EB layer but wrong for champion). For operational-pragmatist champion, the hook must name Ashley's specific tasks, not lead with the percentage. Rewrite names the three manual morning tasks (HD reconciliation, CE rekey, document review — all sage.json documented) as the cost of the baseline, then anchors the McKinsey stat as the benchmark. Stat is preserved as supporting evidence. McKinsey entry is placed last in fomoOrdered[] because its fomoProfileFit = roi-analytical (EB layer), not operational-pragmatist (champion layer).

decisions.default: Lead with sage.json primaryPainQuote as emotional anchor; no skepticism acknowledgment

I feel like I've traveled back to the 90s.'); frame as 'these systems are archaic by design, not by accident' before naming the manual tasks that stop.

decisions.default: null (no explicit weekly job volume in scoping data)

decisions.rationale: Source priority per principle: (a) sage.json volume × lag — no explicit weekly job count in transcripts; (b) sage.json manual hours: 1.5h/job (Ashley's demo, 2026-04-16, sage.json confirmedFlows.UC2) × 5 jobs/week (conservative estimate for 7-location regional contractor) × 26 weeks = 195h. The 5-job/week estimate is conservative and is flagged as an estimate in the sixMonthWindow field with a directive to confirm with Ashley. Figure uses documented per-unit metric (1.5h/job) with an estimated volume — stated as 'conservative floor' not a definitive number. Excludes UC1 (~2.5h/week daily HD reconciliation) and UC3 (~2h/week contract review) which are both documented but lack per-unit quantification. Brian Cook's '$5K/month GCP hosting savings' (sage.json budgetSignals) is infrastructure cost, not integration labor cost — not applicable.

decisions.likelyVendor: Salesforce implementation partner (SI) — Flows/Apex native pitch
decisions.likelyVendorJustification: Peerless has Salesforce active and licensed — the most common competitive threat DataSkate faces in Salesforce-anchored accounts is the incumbent or prospective Salesforce SI offering to build natively in Flows/Apex. This avoids adding MuleSoft licensing cost and appears cheaper upfront. More likely than Boomi (no Salesforce-native pitch), Celigo (CPG/NetSuite focus, no CE expertise), Zapier (too lightweight for legacy ERP writes), or in-house dev (Peerless has no MuleSoft developer; Brian is the Elevate platform IT director, not the integration operator).
decisions.countermeasureJustification: The strongest DataSkate-specific defensive claim is the CE Live Service relay knowledge. No generalist Salesforce SI discovers this CE quirk (production-only API surface, Deltek-managed relay URL, port 445 on the VM, sequential job-number consumption rule) without weeks of discovery. Embedding this finding in the challenge section forces any competing vendor to answer the same question before Peerless engages them — and most cannot answer it.
